name: plaza fountain, 3/4 top-down: round stone basin (rim top seen from above as an elliptical ring, curved ashlar front rim face), water surface with ripple rings inside, central pillar with two tiered bowls (their water seen from above) and a gold eight-point star finial, water streams falling

surfaces.part: main basin rim ring and water surface (elliptical mouth)

answer.evidence: The width profile widens from 35 at row 30 to 61 at row 39, holds at 61 through row 52, then narrows to 23 at row 63. That is a full ellipse. The rim ring runs from the back rim at rows 30-31, with dark inner shadow at rows 32-33. The teal water interior (rows 34-50) is clearly seen from above, and the light front rim line is at rows 51-52. Below it, the curved ashlar front rim face covers rows 53-62, about 10 rows. The two tiered bowls above also show their water surfaces as small ellipses (rows 11-17 and 21-29). The finial and water streams are decor.

styleAnswer.evidence: The candidate carries 14 visible tones per full tile, between the hedge (9) and the stall (17) and well (20), so it is at reference level for a prop of this size. Near-flat coverage is 0%, the same as the well and hedge. Only 4% of dark edge pixels are neutral, so the outline is tinted: dark teal beside water and dark blue-grey beside stone, not a black sticker line. The stone rim shows individually shaded ashlar blocks with light and dark steps. The water has about 4-5 teal steps with ripple rings and highlights. The tiered bowls and falling streams are shaded in several steps, and the gold star finial is clear. I see no large flat fills and nothing that looks thinner or flatter than the well or stall references.
